arithmetic: Foundation Note 5: 116,814,419 + 3,256,393 = 120,070,812 (printed total; also 3,256,393 + 28,617,995 + 88,196,424 = 120,070,812). University-owned: 199,762 (1982 transfer) + 6,000,000 (2023 Department of Education grants) = 6,199,762 (printed as 'Due from Foundation'). No-double-count test: the Foundation's 120,070,812 is a net-asset figure, and the 6,199,762 is one of the Foundation's liabilities (liabilities 7,405,269 + 1,615,624 + 141,163 + 801,106 + 6,199,762 = 16,162,924; 16,162,924 + net assets 203,952,196 = total 220,115,120), so the 6,199,762 is outside every net-asset figure by construction. Supporting test: the 6,000,000 transferred in fiscal 2023 does not appear in the 2023 roll-forward of endowment net assets (105,795,188 + 8,625,825 + 4,268,974 + 15,303 - 6,236,302 + 776,522 = 113,245,510). Combined, without double counting: 120,070,812 + 6,199,762 = 126,270,574. The sum is the verifier's; neither report prints a combined total. Whole dollars as printed.
entity_note: Two audited entities. The University (a component unit of the State of Missouri; Springfield and West Plains campuses, Mountain Grove and Dalian locations) owns the 6,199,762 but holds no endowment investments itself; it carries the amount as a receivable from the Foundation at original principal. The Missouri State University Foundation is a legally separate nonprofit, discretely presented in the University's statements (University Note 1, PDF p. 20), and reports under FASB. The 120,070,812 belongs to the Foundation. UNITID 179566 is the Springfield campus; the unaudited 'Condensed Schedules by Campus' (University report PDF p. 68) put the whole 6,199,762 of nonexpendable net position under Springfield and none under West Plains. The Foundation's endowment is not split by campus in either report.
differences_from_original: Value unchanged (126,270,574; components 6,199,762 and 120,070,812 both confirmed to the dollar, same pages). One change of substance: the first researcher's caveat that 'a small overlap cannot be ruled out' is not supported by the documents. The Foundation's endowment total is a net-asset figure and the University's 6,199,762 sits in the Foundation's liabilities, so the two cannot overlap; the 2023 roll-forward confirms the 6,000,000 was never added to endowment net assets. Earnings on the University's funds are separate dollars that the Foundation records in its own books; they are not part of the 6,199,762. Confidence raised from medium to high on the no-double-count question. Page references in the original are PDF page numbers and are correct.
reader_caveats: 1. The combined figure is an addition across two audited reports, not a printed total. 2. The two components are on different measurement bases: the Foundation figure is endowment net assets at fair value; the University's 6,199,762 is original principal, unchanged from 2023, with no fair value disclosed. 3. The reports say earnings on the University's funds are recorded in the Foundation's books but do not say in which net-asset line, so it is not known whether those earnings are inside the 120,070,812; either way they are counted at most once. 4. Neither report states the gross investments held for endowment; the investment pool for 'funds treated as endowment' is 121,995,631 at market value (Foundation Note 2), which is not the same measure as the 126,270,574 and is not reconciled to it in the documents. 5. IPEDS asks for gross endowment investments including affiliated foundations; on that definition the liability to the University belongs in the total, which supports using 126,270,574 and not the Foundation-only 120,070,812. 6. The University report on the web is a March 2025 re-posting (file name 'Revised0325', PDF modified 2025-03-11) with the auditor's report still dated December 5, 2024; its 'Revision' paragraph (PDF p. 25) covers only an immaterial change to the 2023 Note 17 liquidity disclosure. 7. The Foundation statements are single-year with summarized 2023 comparatives. 8. No going-concern or other emphasis paragraph in either report.
